summary: This program builds a list of Book objects, sorts it several different ways using Comparator, and then compares two sets of book titles to find their intersection, union, and difference.

lines.text: Brings in the whole java.util package, which supplies List, ArrayList, Comparator, Set, HashSet, and Arrays all at once.
Declares the variable by the List interface but creates an ArrayList, so the code depends on the general contract rather than one particular implementation.

lines.code: books.add(new Book("The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes", "Arthur Conan Doyle", "Mystery"));
lines.text: Adds a Book to the end of the list; the three arguments match the title, author, and genre the Book constructor expects.
The enhanced for loop walks the list in order, giving each element the name b for the body of the loop.
Printing an object calls its toString method, which is why Book needs a readable toString for this output to be useful.
Sorts the list in place. Comparator.comparing builds a comparator from a key, and Book::getTitle is a method reference meaning "call getTitle on each book to get that key."
The \n escape adds a blank line before the heading so each section of output is visually separated.
The same list is re-sorted using a different key, showing that the ordering lives in the comparator, not in the list.
Starts a two-level sort with genre as the primary key.
Chains a tiebreaker: books that share a genre are then ordered by title.
A Set holds no duplicates and has no guaranteed order. Arrays.asList wraps the listed titles so the HashSet constructor can copy them in.
Copies myTitles first, because the set operations that follow modify the set they are called on and would otherwise destroy the original.
Keeps only the elements that also appear in friendTitles, leaving the titles both people own.
Adds every title from the friend's set; because a set rejects duplicates, shared titles appear only once.
Strips out everything the friend also has, leaving the titles unique to my collection.
